inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: Q2 2026 10-Q diluted weighted-average 594.0M (cover-page basic 594.08M at 2026-07-17; dilutive securities are immaterial, <0.5M). Held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows. Standalone model: the ~1 UNP share per NS share issuance under the pending Norfolk Southern merger is NOT modelled.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense $142M (SEC XBRL companyfacts). Tax withheld on net-share settlement is not separately tagged in XBRL; at ~0.6% of revenue SBC is immaterial to value either way.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Rf 4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.0 -> cost of equity ~9.2%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~4.6% (A-rated; FY25 interest $1,309M on ~$32B debt = 4.1% book), ~3.6% after 22% tax. Market weights: equity ~$165B, net debt ~$28.7B -> D/V ~15%. WACC ~8.4%, used 8.25% (one rate for all scenarios; cyclicality is charged in the bear scenario and the 20% bear weight, not by a WACC premium).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP single treatment: operating-lease cost ($305M FY25) sits inside operating expenses, so EBITDA is already post-lease; operating-lease liabilities ($1.0B) are therefore NOT in net debt. Finance leases ($105M) are inside total debt.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (routing table: mature US operating company; cyclical industrial - freight volumes track industrial production/trade, so no WACC premium but a 20% bear weight and a cap below Gordon). Not a REIT/bank/holdco. STANDALONE UNP: the pending ~$85B Norfolk Southern acquisition (announced 2025-07-29; STB procedural schedule adopted 2026-08-18; targeted close late 2027; opposed by BNSF, CSX, shipper coalitions, labor, farm groups, DOJ Antitrust) is not modelled - no NS revenue, synergies, ~225M new shares, ~$20B+ acquisition debt or assumed NS debt. If it closes, the leverage and share-count inputs here are superseded and the valuation must be rebuilt on a combined basis. Merger agreement carries a reverse termination fee payable by UNP on regulatory failure (reported ~$2.5B, ~$4/share; not verified against the filing here, not in the bridge). Buybacks: historically a large repurchaser ($2.7B FY25, $6-8B/yr FY18-22) but effectively paused since the NS announcement ($26M H1-26) - the flat count is currently a modelling convention, not being funded. Other income ($629M FY25: real-estate sales, rents, pension credit) is excluded from the flows and no matching asset is added - a conservative omission of roughly $0.5B/yr. Owner FCF = reported FCF $5,499M - SBC $142M - interest income 0 (net-debt company, no deduction). Reported FCF is after ~$1.3B interest; the engine projects unlevered FCF and deducts net debt once.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: forward nominal revenue growth (core pricing above rail inflation + low-single-digit volume); equity CAGR rejected
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is not usable: book equity fell from $21.2B (FY2014) to $12.2B (FY2022) on ~$45B of buybacks, then rebuilt as buybacks slowed, so the 3y equity CAGR (14.9%) and 5y (1.7%) describe capital return, not compounding. 5y revenue/EPS CAGRs start at the FY2020 COVID trough. 10y revenue CAGR is only 1.2% (coal decline offset pricing).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGR is slightly below reported FCF CAGR (SBC grew from $73M to $142M FY20-25) but SBC is <0.6% of revenue, so the gap is immaterial. EPS growth over the decade came mainly from margin (OR ~63% -> ~60%) and a ~32% share-count reduction, not from revenue.

base.growth_rationale: FY26 +6%: H1-26 revenue +7.4% (Q2 +12% on fuel surcharge, pricing, bulk +12%/industrial +4% volumes) against soft international intermodal/auto. Then core pricing ~3% plus ~0.5-1% volume, fading to 3% nominal.
base.margin_rationale: Adj. EBITDA (pre-SBC) = OI + D&A + SBC: FY25 50.8%, H1-26 50.1% (fuel surcharge inflates revenue and dilutes the ratio). Guidance is continued OR improvement; base takes OR from ~60% to ~58.7% over six years.
base.tax_note: Cash tax low in FY26 (H1-26 cash taxes $236M vs $785M H1-25) on 100% bonus depreciation restored mid-2025; ramps to the ~22% book rate (federal + state) by year 6 so the deferral is not perpetuated.

scenario_narratives.base: Standalone UNP keeps doing what it has done for a decade: core pricing a little above rail cost inflation, volumes flat to low-single-digit as bulk (grain, renewable feedstocks) and domestic-intermodal truck conversion offset tariff-hit international intermodal and soft autos, and PSR discipline under Vena grinding the operating ratio from ~60% toward ~58.5%. Capex stays ~14.5% of revenue, the bonus-depreciation cash-tax holiday unwinds to ~22%, and revenue compounds ~3.5%. The NS merger is treated as outside the model: neither the synergies nor the leverage.
scenario_narratives.bull: Durable duopoly pricing plus a truck-to-rail conversion cycle (tight truck capacity, UP's service metrics at records) lift volume growth to 2-3% on top of pricing, and further PSR/automation cost-out (fuel efficiency, terminal automation, asset velocity) takes the OR toward ~55.5%, at or past the best in the industry. Capex intensity drifts down as velocity gains free locomotives and cars. Revenue compounds ~5% early, 3.5% terminal.
scenario_narratives.bear: A tariff-driven freight recession in 2027 (international intermodal, autos, chemicals) drops revenue ~1% and the OR back above 62% as volume deleverage meets a unionized cost base and a two-person-crew floor on headcount savings. Recovery is slow; captive-shipper rate scrutiny and post-merger-fight regulatory hostility (STB, DOJ, labor) cap pricing, so growth settles at 2.5% with margins ~3pp below today and capex stickier at 15%. Merger distraction or a failed deal (with a reverse termination fee) adds to the drag.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): freight volumes are cyclical and tariff-exposed and the NS fight raises regulatory and management-distraction risk on the standalone business. Base 55%: a decade of flat-volume, pricing-plus-OR execution is the most likely path. Bull 25% (below 35%): it needs volume growth and further OR gains to arrive together, which has not happened in this industry for years.

valuation_philosophy.summary: UNP is a mature, irreplaceable network with pricing power and a stable ~50% EBITDA margin, valued on standalone unlevered owner FCF at an 8.25% USD WACC. Value is driven by the margin path (OR) and nominal pricing, not volume. The pending Norfolk Southern merger is deliberately excluded; it is a binary catalyst that would change leverage, share count and the growth profile.
key_risks_to_valuation: NS merger: if approved, ~225M new shares, ~$20B+ new debt plus assumed NS debt and multi-year integration risk (UP/SP 1996-98 service meltdown precedent) supersede this standalone model; if rejected, a reverse termination fee and lost management time
Freight recession / tariffs: international intermodal and autos already down; volume deleverage moves the OR quickly
Regulatory/labor: two-person crew rule, captive-shipper rate cases, post-East Palestine safety politics limit cost-out
Cash-tax normalisation: the bonus-depreciation deferral is assumed to unwind to ~22%; a permanent lower cash rate would add value
Terminal value is ~70%+ of EV; each 50bp of WACC moves value ~8-10%
